items.t: Brake pedal sinks or brakes fail from a leaking master cylinder
items.job: Replace brake master cylinder and bleed brakes

items.t: Valve cover gasket and spark plug well oil leaks
items.job: Replace valve cover gasket and spark plug tube seals

items.t: Distributor failure causes rough idle or no-start
items.note: A new OEM-style distributor is about $250; used units cost much less but are a gamble.

items.t: Check engine light for evaporative system codes
items.job: Replace EVAP purge valve or clear blocked vent line
items.note: Often the fix is just a tight gas cap or clearing a blocked vent line.

items.t: Weak A/C from a cracked low-pressure hose
items.job: Replace A/C low-pressure hose, evacuate and recharge

items.t: Check engine light for misfire code P0300
items.job: Replace spark plugs (and wires if worn)

items.t: Timing chain guide breaks and rattles
items.job: Replace timing chain, tensioner and guides
items.note: KBB lists about $2,428–$2,652 at a dealer. If only the upper guide is broken and caught early, replacing it through the valve cover costs far less.

items.t: Check engine light for airflow sensor code P0100
items.note: KBB lists about $576–$658 at a dealer. Have the wiring tested first.

items.t: Engine surges at stops with the A/C on
items.note: YourMechanic quotes about $364 for 1996–1997. Cleaning the valve and throttle body first costs much less.

items.t: Parking brake does not hold on a hill
items.note: YourMechanic quotes about $95–$115 for the adjustment. Worn rear brake parts or a stretched cable cost extra.

items.t: Fuel tank leaks and gas smell
items.note: The inspection is about $95 (YourMechanic). A new genuine Nissan tank is about $454–$601 for the part alone, plus labor to drop and refit the tank.

items.t: Airbags may not deploy or may go off unexpectedly
items.note: About $95–$115 to find the fault (YourMechanic). Sensors, the airbag module or dash repairs after a deployment cost extra.
